correctness.rationale: For rank-one \(A=u\varphi\) and involution U, \(AU\) remains rank one and is nilpotent iff its trace vanishes, so factorizations are exactly involutions satisfying \(\varphi(Uu)=0\). Similarity and nonzero scaling reduce the trace-zero and nonzero-trace strata to \(E_{12}\) and \(E_{11}\). In odd characteristic, writing \(U=I-2P\) converts the problem to an idempotent incidence count; in characteristic two, \(U=I+S\) with \(S^2=0\) and rank at most one gives the analogous square-zero incidence count. Inclusion-exclusion and projective rescaling yield the four stated polynomials. Independent brute-force enumeration over all 3x3 matrices for q=2 and q=3 reproduced (14,6) and (128,48).

originality.rationale: Mabilat's complete current paper characterizes existence of nilpotent--involution factorizations over arbitrary fields and explicitly remarks that the decomposition is generally nonunique, including examples, but it does not count factorizations. The audited result turns that open multiplicity dimension into an exact finite-field incidence law on the natural rank-one M3 stratum, with a nontrivial characteristic and trace dichotomy. Resultary and targeted searches found no prior equivalent formula.
